title: add-benchmark-lab-adaptive-batching-reporting-pipeline-v115
author: Anika Rao
description:
Add adaptive batching reporting pipeline and representative workload runners

Motivation: We need a standardized reporting pipeline to collect per-batch latency, effective batch size, KV-cache hit rates, and model-variant cost metrics for the adaptive-batching project. This PR introduces a pipeline that ingests raw runner traces, aggregates metrics by model/variant/hardware, and publishes summaries to the benchmark-lab reporting store so dashboards and alerting can consume them.

What this PR does:
- Adds pipeline orchestration definition for adaptive batching reporting (airflow-compatible YAML)
- Implements a collector and aggregator for adaptive-batching traces with dedup/rollup and latency histograms
- Adds representative workload runner (seq2seq and chat-mix) adapters that emit the new trace schema
- Updates CI to run the benchmark-lab smoke test and adds an infra Terraform change to provision the reporting topic
- Adds docs and an example dashboard query

Notes:
- The description below contains the full checklist and links to Linear tickets. The collector has retries and backoff; aggregator uses time-windowed bucketing to align with existing reporting windows.

Checklist:
- [x] Pipeline orchestration (benchmark-lab/pipelines/adaptive_batching/reporting_pipeline.yaml)
- [x] Collector implementation (benchmark-lab/collectors/adaptive_batching/collector.py)
- [x] Aggregator + rollup (benchmark-lab/collectors/adaptive_batching/aggregator.py)
- [x] Representative runners updated (benchmark-lab/workloads/representative_runners/*)
- [x] CI smoke tests and example job (ci/benchmark-lab.yml)
- [x] Docs and README update (docs/benchmark-lab/README.md)

Related tasks:
- Linear: ENG-5843, ENG-5901
- Support follow-up (optional): SUP-2211

Impact: Enables per-variant cost/latency tracking for adaptive batching experiments and provides the data source for the v2 dashboard and alerting. No breaking API changes to public SDKs.

Merge strategy: squash and merge to keep history focused on pipeline feature set.
